sources: Campbell, J. F. Popular Tales of the West Highlands. Vol. Iii. Edinburgh: Edmonston and Douglas, 1862, 295+.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Oscar, named Osgar in some tellings, is an Irish and Scottish hero. His father was the poet Oisín; his mother was Eibhir, a mortal woman. The great hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill was his grandfather. Oscar entered the Fianna, the warrior band around Fionn, in the steps of his father. His name, meaning deer lover, points to his grandmother Sadb, once changed into a deer. Oscar led the fiercest of the Fianna fighters. He led the band nicknamed the terrible broom, for it swept a battlefield bare. After his grandfather died, Oscar became leader of the band. At the battle of Gabhra, where the Fianna were defeated, Oscar slew the enemy’s high king Cairbre and then perished from wounds he took in the same fight. His wife Aidín grieved herself to death after Oisín, his father, carried him into the Otherworld.

okr.objective: Oscar is the fiercest Fianna hero and grandson of Fionn.
key_results: Oscar was the son of the poet Oisín and the grandson of Fionn Mac Cumhaill.
